Before answering, one comparability note: Alaska Air Group's FY2024 results include Hawaiian Holdings only from the September 18, 2024 acquisition date onward (a partial-year, ~3.5-month contribution), whereas Delta, United, Southwest, and American report full twelve-month results on a consistent standalone basis [DOC-2]. This makes Alaska's reported profitability not fully comparable to the other four "as businesses," though it does not change the ranking outcome below.

Using net income as the primary profitability measure for FY2024 (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2024, per each company's 10-K):
- Delta Air Lines: Net income $3,457M [DOC-1]
- United Airlines Holdings: Net income $3,149M [DOC-1]
- American Airlines Group: Net income $846M [DOC-1]
- Southwest Airlines: Net income $465M [DOC-1]
- Alaska Air Group: Net income $395M (partial-year Hawaiian contribution of a $113M net loss included) [DOC-1][DOC-2]

Delta also leads on operating income ($5,995M vs. United's $5,096M, American's $2,614M, Alaska's $570M, and Southwest's $321M) [DOC-1]. By both operating income and net income, Delta Air Lines was the most profitable of the five in FY2024.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines
